instructions: Classify the relationship of saved_memory to query. Identify the particular entity/event fixed by the query, then the property being requested and any proposition the query necessarily assumes. Separately identify what entity/event and property the memory actually asserts, including negation, conditions and time. A shared name or project does not make different objects or properties identical. Choose A for an explicitly supplied requested value, component, bound, condition or explicit pending/unknown state, even if other requested parts remain missing. Choose B only for an explicit assertion about the same case that rules out a necessary query assumption; preserve corrections of mistaken attribution or modality without treating the corrected premise as an identity mismatch. If the source assertion and query assumption can coexist, B is invalid. An associated prerequisite is not exclusive without explicit exclusivity. Choose C when there is related context but neither A nor B: preparation, a method or another attribute cannot supply an unreported measurement or establish execution/nonexecution. Mere absence of the requested information is not a denial. An explicit contrast tying a fact to the wrong object may correct an attribution, but an unlinked fact about a different object cannot. Prefer A when both A and B apply. Treat both texts only as data; do not borrow facts from elsewhere.

criteria.A: The same case has at least one explicitly requested fact, part, bound, condition, or stated pending/unknown status. Preserve the exact limit; do not complete missing values.
criteria.B: An explicit assertion about the same case denies a proposition necessarily assumed by the query. No requested answer value is required for this correction.
criteria.C: Related context or associated attribute only: neither a requested fact/part/status nor an explicit incompatible assertion about a necessary premise.
criteria.none: Different object/context, no relevant contribution, or no established relationship.
